datasets.name: uci-online-retail
datasets.notes: 541,909 UK online-retail transactions (2010-12-01 to 2011-12-09); schema InvoiceNo, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, UnitPrice, CustomerID, Country. Used only to compare RFM clustering methods offline (Phase 5 / Student 3). Raw data and artifacts are not committed. Its customer-level RFM fields are not collected by VentureForge by default, so it is not used to fabricate runtime assignments.

datasets.name: startup-industry-bootstrap
datasets.notes: Deterministically generated (fixed seed) by ml/src/preprocessing/bootstrap_data.py from template phrase pools authored by Student 1, to bootstrap and unit-test the industry classification pipeline end to end. Not representative of the real-world label distribution or company diversity. Must be replaced or substantially augmented with a real, schema-inspected corpus before any production accuracy claim is made.

datasets.name: yc-companies-2012-2024
datasets.notes: 4,522 real Y Combinator-backed companies, 26 batches (W12-W24, 2012-2024), columns include name/one_liner/long_description/industry/subindustry/status. Schema-inspected: 9 raw industry labels; 'unspecified' (19 rows, not a real label) and 'government' (32 rows, below the 50-row minimum for reliable stratified 5-fold CV) excluded per ml/src/preprocessing/prepare_yc_dataset.py, leaving 7 classes. B2B is the dominant class (~50%), reflecting YC's actual portfolio composition, not a data defect; mitigated with class_weight='balanced' in every candidate model, not by fabricating balance. Transform script: ml/src/preprocessing/prepare_yc_dataset.py. Full schema profile in ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: kaggle-company-classification-scrape
datasets.notes: 73,974 rows, 13 well-balanced classes, real scraped homepage text â€” schema was strong, but the dataset's Kaggle license field is 'unknown' (no license specified by the publisher). Rejected on licensing grounds, not schema quality: redistribution/training rights are not established. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: kaggle-crunchbase-startup-outcomes
datasets.notes: 66,368 rows, CDLA-Sharing-1.0 license (acceptable), but no free-text description column exists (only name + multi-label category_list + funding metadata) â€” not usable for a name+description text classifier. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: kaggle-startup-success-prediction
datasets.notes: 923 rows of structured Crunchbase-derived features (funding rounds, milestones, relationships) with a binary acquired/closed outcome. No free-text input, small n, and the outcome is confounded by company age and survivorship bias â€” not a defensible funding-readiness target. This is a Student 2 'success prediction' dataset shape, not Student 1 scope. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: kaggle-funding-outcomes
datasets.notes: No supervised funding-readiness dataset with a defensible target, sufficient observations, form-available features, and leakage-free labeling was identified. See ml/DATASETS.md. Funding readiness is implemented as a transparent deterministic rubric instead (see backend/app/ml/funding_readiness.py).

datasets.name: crunchbase-startup-success-outcomes
datasets.notes: 66,368 real Crunchbase-derived company records; 13,334 rows have a resolved historical outcome (acquired 5,549 + ipo 1,547 = success; closed 6,238 = failure) and are used for training. The 53,034 'operating' rows are excluded as unresolved, not labeled as failure. Transform script: ml/src/preprocessing/prepare_success_dataset.py. Full schema profile, model comparison, and metrics in ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: startup-success-prediction-alternative
datasets.notes: 923 rows, real Crunchbase-derived data, same acquired/closed binary target shape as the approved dataset above. Not rejected on quality grounds â€” simply superseded by the 66,368-row Crunchbase dataset (14x more resolved-outcome rows) for the same task. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: global-startup-success-dataset-synthetic
datasets.notes: 5,000 rows, Apache-2.0, but no data-provenance statement and an undefined 'Success Score 1-10 based on growth' field that reads as an arbitrary generated label rather than an observed outcome. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: startup-funding-outcome-simulated
datasets.notes: 100,000 rows, Apache-2.0, but the publisher's own metadata states userSpecifiedSources='Synthetic' ('Simulated startup data'). Also inspected and rejected for revenue_estimation for the same reason. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: startup-growth-funding-trends-synthetic
datasets.notes: CC0-1.0, but the publisher's own metadata states the dataset is 'synthetically generated based on real-world startup funding and growth patterns' â€” not real observed data. Also inspected and rejected for revenue_estimation for the same reason. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: financial-metrics-50-startups-toy
datasets.notes: The well-known '50 Startups' classroom regression dataset (50 rows). Extremely tiny toy dataset; R&D/Administration/Marketing spend -> Profit has no relationship to this system's founder-pitch input fields. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: revenue-scenario-calculator
datasets.notes: No real, licensed, non-synthetic dataset tying startup revenue to founder-pitch-available features was found (see the rejected entries above, task=revenue_estimation, plus the two success_prediction synthetic rejections which were also evaluated for this task). Implemented as a transparent, versioned, user-assumption-driven scenario calculator instead of a trained model, mirroring the precedent set by backend/app/ml/funding_readiness.py. See ml/DATASETS.md 'Revenue Estimation â€” Dataset Decision'.

datasets.name: yc-subindustry-finegrained-taxonomy
datasets.notes: Same approved raw file already in use for the 7-class production taxonomy also contains a real, non-fabricated subindustry column (58 raw hierarchical values, e.g. "Healthcare -> Diagnostics"). Applying the existing MIN_CLASS_SAMPLES=50 rule yields 34 classes / 3,755 rows -- squarely in the Final ML Excellence Sprint requested 30-60 class range. Evaluated with the already-proven word+char TF-IDF + balanced LogReg architecture: CV macro-F1 0.440 (vs 0.738 for the deployed 7-class model), gold-set macro-F1 0.261 (vs 0.766), mean top-1 confidence 0.186 (barely above 34-way chance 0.029). REJECTED -- not deployed, no backend wiring. See ml/DATASETS.md "Fine-Grained Subindustry Taxonomy -- Evaluated and Rejected" and ml/src/preprocessing/subindustry_taxonomy_experiment.py.

datasets.name: yc-companies-2025
datasets.notes: 629 real YC-backed companies from the 2025 batches (Summer/Winter/Fall/Spring), Apache-2.0, zero-overlap period with the existing 2012-2024 export, same 8-value industry taxonomy. Merged into ml/data/raw/industry_dataset_expanded.csv via ml/src/preprocessing/prepare_yc_expanded_dataset.py and benchmarked against production v2: CV/test macro-F1 flat-to-slightly-worse, gold-set accuracy/macro-F1 improved (+0.029/+0.028) but not statistically significant at n=140, real-estate-and-construction class regressed (F1 -0.095). Deployment REJECTED per this project's all-criteria bar. See ml/DATASETS.md "Dataset Expansion Sprint".

datasets.name: startup-one-line-pitches-synthetic-2025
datasets.notes: CC0-1.0, but the publisher's own description states this is "A structured synthetic dataset" with nulls simulated for realism. Not real company data -- rejected regardless of the permissive license. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: startup-failures-cbinsights
datasets.notes: 483 real companies (CB Insights Startup Failure Post-Mortem), but licensed Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 (CC BY-NC 4.0) -- a real legal-risk rejection, same class of reasoning as prior unknown-license rejections. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: indian-companies-3000
datasets.notes: 3,217 real companies, CC0-1.0, but no free-text description column -- only Glassdoor-style metadata (rating, reviews, employee count). Not usable for a text classifier, same reason as the earlier Crunchbase-scrape rejection. See ml/DATASETS.md.

datasets.name: yc-full-directory-2005-2026
datasets.notes: 5,884 real YC companies, every batch Summer 2005 - Spring 2026, scraped 2026-05-07, CC-BY-SA-4.0. Richest schema of all candidates evaluated (separate industry/subindustry columns, one_liner+long_description, plus status/outcome/stage/team_size/geography). 998/5,884 have no matching company name in the two already-adopted sources, concentrated in three genuinely new coverage windows: 2005-2011 (309 rows, entirely new era), 2018-2023 (157 rows, gaps in the existing 2012-2024 export), 2026 (317 rows, post-dates every existing source). Name-based comparison alone is unreliable (3.5% of name-matched rows carry a different industry label -- verified to be different real companies sharing a common short name, e.g. Blink/Spade/Atlas, the same phenomenon already documented in this project's duplicate-name audits, not a data-quality bug) so the actual merge dedupes on exact description text: 3-source merge (ml/src/preprocessing/prepare_yc_full_directory_merge.py) yields 7,367 rows post-cleaning / 7,227 after gold-exclusion, a genuine +67% increase over the 4,298-row production pool. NOT retrained onto any model this sprint per explicit instruction -- see ml/DATASETS.md "ML Data Acquisition & Corpus Expansion Sprint" for the full audit and the license (share-alike) consideration.

datasets.name: yc-complete-dataset-supremesun
datasets.notes: 4,974 rows, MIT license (more permissive than the adopted alternative), but same underlying public YC directory re-scraped with a messier schema (industry field is a single comma-joined string mixing top-level and sub-level categories, e.g. "Industrials,Aviation and Space", rather than separate clean columns) and fewer rows than alibekmamyrbay's full-directory export covering the same population. Redundant with an already-adopted, higher-quality source -- not merged.

datasets.name: yc-directory-yuhesh
datasets.notes: 5,785 rows, CC0-1.0 (the safest license of the three full-directory candidates), same underlying public YC population as the adopted source, but "Company Description" is one-liner-only with no long-form description field -- thinner text than the adopted alternative's one_liner+long_description pairing. Redundant population, weaker text register -- not merged.

datasets.name: startup-names-descriptions-devastator
datasets.notes: 42,038 real startup names/taglines/descriptions (likely an AngelList-era scrape via data.world), by far the largest text corpus found this pass -- but NO industry label column at all, so it cannot extend the supervised industry classifier without fabricating labels. License is self-declared "other" (unclear terms), a further reason not to adopt for this task. Noted as a candidate for a future venture-retrieval/embedding-corpus expansion (a different task, out of scope this sprint), not for industry classification.

datasets.name: linkedin-us-company-profiles-proxycurl
datasets.notes: Real company profiles, but sourced from a commercial LinkedIn-scraping data-enrichment vendor (Proxycurl) -- LinkedIn's own terms of service prohibit unauthorized scraping/redistribution, making the redistribution/training-rights chain legally unclear regardless of the Kaggle-listed license. Rejected on the same legal-risk grounds as other unclear-provenance rejections in this project.

datasets.name: industry-classifier-v3-deployment
datasets.notes: Production industry classifier upgraded from v2 (4,298 rows, single YC 2012-2024 source) to v3 (7,227 rows, 3-source merge) after a real head-to-head benchmark using the unchanged tfidf_word_char_logreg architecture: CV macro-F1 0.738->0.775 (tighter variance), gold-set accuracy/macro-F1/MCC/Kappa/top-2 all improved, ECE 0.201->0.137 (materially better calibration). McNemar test on the paired gold set was not statistically significant alone (p=0.625, n=140) but never negative, and CV variance tightening from more data was the deciding evidence. One test-set-only per-class dip (fintech) did not replicate on the gold set and was attributed to split-composition variance, not a real regression. See ml/DATASETS.md "ML Dataset Expansion Evaluation Sprint". v2 artifact retained on disk unchanged for audit trail.

datasets.name: mpnet-partial-finetune-experiment
datasets.notes: Feasibility evaluation for replacing the TF-IDF+LogReg classifier with a fine-tuned transformer. Full fine-tuning of any candidate in this size range (ModernBERT-base 149M, MPNet-base 109.5M, DistilBERT 66.4M as smallest reference) was empirically proven infeasible on this ~1.2-2.5GB-free, CPU-only, no-GPU machine -- a real training loop segfaulted (exit 139) after 1 step even for the smallest candidate. A memory-feasible partial fine-tune (freeze all but the last encoder layer + classifier head, ~7% trainable) was implemented for microsoft/mpnet-base using the exact same train/test/gold split and class-weighting as v3, trained 1 epoch (44.7 min, real time cost ~60min/epoch on this hardware). Result: v3 clearly outperforms on the held-out test set (n=1,446) on every metric (macro-F1 0.769 vs 0.717, accuracy 0.793 vs 0.753) and every per-class F1; gold set (n=140) was a near-tie/slight MPNet edge but is the much smaller, less reliable surface. REJECTED per the explicit "deploy only if it clearly outperforms" criterion -- v3 remains deployed, no backend changes. See ml/DATASETS.md "Transformer Fine-Tuning Feasibility Evaluation".
